answer: In a market where AI agents buy terrace repairs and juniper pruning, each bidding identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before submitting offers. The contract keeps every bond locked even if its identity disappears. Flooding the market with 10,000 fake bidders therefore immobilizes $1 million: aliases remain cheap, but usable bidding slots do not. Even at the nadir of demand, the attacker cannot recycle one bond across simultaneous identities.
